conventions.text: Municipal signs and notices marked the streets where hawkers were not allowed to trade.
source: Roots (NHB collection): Chinese 'Hawkers Prohibited' sign by Singapore Municipal Commission, 1950

conventions.text: Licensed mobile stalls showed their hawker licence on the stall itself.
source: Roots (NHB collection): postcard of a mobile tea stall with licence displayed, c. 1970

conventions.text: Hawkers had to name their stalls once they moved into hawker centres in the 1970s; the usual pattern is a name plus the food sold, and well-known stalls that open new branches often name the place where they first did well.
source: Social Sciences (MDPI), June 2023: What Is Your Legacy? Naming practices of legacy hawker stalls

conventions.text: Older stall signboards are bright and busy: the stall name in big Chinese characters with the English name below, photos of the dishes, and a price for each dish.
source: Rice Media: Hawker Signboards: Hello Minimalism, Goodbye Neon, 30 August 2017

conventions.text: Some newer stalls use plain, cafe-style signboards, a few with no photos or prices at all.
source: Rice Media: Hawker Signboards: Hello Minimalism, Goodbye Neon, 30 August 2017

conventions.text: Most stalls show their prices; in a 2015 survey 89 of 584 stalls did not, more than half of them mixed vegetable rice stalls.
Some stalls sell one dish in two to four sizes at stepped prices, for example wanton noodles at $4.50, $5.50, $6.50 or $8.50.
source: Eatbook: Hong Lim Food Centre guide, 9 January 2025

conventions.text: Extras are priced on their own, for example an extra egg for 50 cents or more cockles for $2 on a plate of char kway teow.
source: Seth Lui: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee, updated 4 December 2025

conventions.text: Takeaway charges ran from 10 to 50 cents, depending on the container: plastic bag, styrofoam box or plastic box.
Many hawkers charge 20 to 30 cents extra for a takeaway container.
source: Dollars and Sense: Sustainable Package Practices, 23 January 2023

conventions.text: Many stalls put up a sign giving the extra charge for takeaway; at the new Bukit Canberra centre most charged 30 to 50 cents until the operator capped it at 30 cents.
A takeaway drink costs more than one served at the stall: one soya bean milk stall charged 80 cents for a glass and $1.40 in a paper cup.
Newer hawker centres serve dine-in meals on reusable plates and bowls only, and since September 2018 new stallholders at older NEA centres cannot use disposables for dine-in either.
source: NEA reply in The Straits Times, 19 June 2019

conventions.text: Stallholders had to display their hygiene grade, from A (best) to D, where diners could see it.
source: BiblioAsia: Hawkers: From Public Nuisance to National Icons, 2013

conventions.text: Every licensed stall displays a licence decal with a QR code that links to its hygiene record.
source: NEA reply in The Straits Times, 19 December 2018

conventions.text: Grades A, B or C now reflect a stall's food safety track record, with NEW for stalls under a year old; diners check the grade by scanning the QR code on the SFA licence at the stall.
Halal-certified stalls display a MUIS halal certificate; showing the MUIS halal logo without a valid certificate is an offence.
A 'no pork, no lard' sign is not halal certification; halal covers more than leaving out pork and lard.
New MUIS halal certificates carry a QR code that diners can scan to check the certification is real and still valid.
Stalls in HPB's Healthier Dining Programme tag lighter dishes with a 'lower in calories' label, and drink stalls show reminders to ask for less or no sugar.
One SGQR label at the stall replaces several separate payment QR codes and works with many apps, including PayNow, NETS and GrabPay.
A unified e-payment scheme for hawker centres, with NETS as the acquirer, started in June 2019, and stallholders could earn up to $1,500 in bonuses for using it.
source: IMDA and Enterprise Singapore factsheet: Hawkers Go Digital, June 2020

conventions.text: Stalls that take CDC vouchers show a CDC Vouchers decal at the stall front.
source: CDC Vouchers Scheme media release, 25 January 2021

conventions.text: At socially-conscious enterprise hawker centres, every stall offers at least one value meal at a lower price, alongside its other dishes.
source: MSE written reply to a parliamentary question, 3 February 2026

conventions.text: Drink orders use short codes: kopi O is black coffee with sugar, kopi O kosong has no sugar, and adding peng makes it iced.
